title: Japanese household consumption and worker income contract in real terms despite nominal stability
source_unit: Japan Statistics Bureau Family Income and Expenditure Survey, July 2026, two-or-more-person households

denominator.unit: average monthly household account; survey estimate, not national aggregate spending

observations.method: Japan Statistics Bureau Family Income and Expenditure Survey monthly result for two-or-more-person households; real changes are deflated using the survey's consumer-price treatment and the release reports both nominal and real movements.
observations.uncertainty: This is a sample survey of household accounts, not a full national-accounts measure. The July estimate is a monthly cross-section, subject to sampling and non-sampling error; the survey's 2025 questionnaire/classification revisions and price-base treatment matter for comparisons.
observations.subgroup: Two-or-more-person households in Japan; no direct one-person-household estimate in this observation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A real decline can reflect temporary timing, weather, prices, household composition, or category-specific substitution rather than a durable fall in cultural or discretionary demand; the average conceals distribution across households.

denominator.unit: average monthly workers' household account; survey estimate

observations.method: Japan Statistics Bureau Family Income and Expenditure Survey monthly result for workers' households; the worker-household income series is reported separately from two-or-more-person household consumption.
observations.uncertainty: The income measure is an average for the worker-household subgroup and does not establish wage composition, hours, employment transitions, debt, transfers, or disposable-income changes. The cross-sectional monthly comparison does not identify household trajectories.
observations.subgroup: Workers' households in Japan; household classification and income definition follow the Statistics Bureau survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Real worker-household income can fall while some groups gain through bonuses, transfers, or employment changes; the aggregate does not establish why consumption changed or whether households reduced saving, quantity, quality, or cultural spending.

related_sources.claim: Official monthly Japanese release page lists the July 2026 two-or-more-person household real consumption result and time-series context.
Official Statistics Bureau Q&A documents sampling-error treatment and the survey's tabulated-household context.

boundary: This record adds a household-account layer beneath aggregate national spending and establishment sales. It does not isolate cultural or leisure categories in July, identify individual households, establish causality, measure one-person households, or prove that real consumption contraction equals reduced wellbeing.
